sources.title: W. W. Hager, “Runge-Kutta methods in optimal control and the transformed adjoint system,” Numerische Mathematik 87 (2000)
sources.locator: Complete 36-page paper retrieved. Read §§1–5, printed pp. 247–271, and §7, printed pp. 277–280.

read_evidence.method: Complete full-text document retrieved and the complete cited sections and their derivations inspected.
read_evidence.scope: Full §§1–5 on continuous and discrete optimal-control formulations, Runge–Kutta transcription, transformed discrete adjoints, and convergence; and §7 on error analysis. The article’s additional optimal-control order conditions were read in full.

contents.name: §2, finite-horizon optimal-control problem and continuous adjoint system
contents.support: Provides the finite-horizon state, cost, Hamiltonian, and adjoint conventions used by the continuous LQR definition and adjoint items.

contents.name: §3, Runge–Kutta discretization and transformed discrete adjoint
contents.support: Supports the stage-map transcription and explains why discrete adjoints need optimal-control-specific consistency analysis.

contents.name: §3, general Runge–Kutta stage equations
contents.support: Provides the stage-equation form, including coupled implicit stages that the local definition uses as NLP variables rather than solving during construction.

contents.name: §3, directional derivative identity for the continuous and discrete objectives
contents.support: Supports the adjoint-gradient route; the local item supplies the complete quadratic expansion and integration-by-parts proof.

contents.name: §4, Runge–Kutta order conditions for optimal-control discretizations
contents.support: Shows that ordinary ODE tableau order is not by itself an optimal-control convergence theorem; the local result therefore assumes uniform objective consistency and recovery.

contents.name: §5, convergence of discrete optimal solutions under consistency hypotheses
contents.support: Motivates conditional conversion of objective consistency and optimization gap into control error; the explicit constants are derived locally.

contents.name: §7, convergence and error estimates for Runge–Kutta optimal control
contents.support: Records the source’s stronger discretization hypotheses as context; this item does not claim a rate or discrete-adjoint estimate absent those hypotheses.

contents.name: §13.3, multiple shooting and direct collocation

contents.name: §13.4, NLP solvers for direct optimal-control transcriptions
